object.title: Exceptional-value conjecture for self-conjugate 6- and 4-core counts
object.statement:
Let $sc_t(n)$ denote the number of self-conjugate $t$-core partitions of $n$, and let $n$ be an integer with $n>15$. **Exceptional-value conjecture for self-conjugate 6- and 4-core counts.**

$$
sc_6(n)<sc_4(n)
$$

when $n\in\{112,180,265\}$, while

$$
sc_6(n)=sc_4(n)
$$

when $n\in\{27,28,33,40,73,75,118,190,248\}$. The source reports this as a computation-assisted conjectural description and further conjectures that the set of integers with $sc_6(n)\leq sc_4(n)$ is finite.
object.source_name: Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Rishi Nath, “The number of self-conjugate core partitions”, arXiv:1201.6629 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.6629

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2012). “We state this as an open question.”

object.title: Unimodality conjecture for normalized self-conjugate core increments
object.statement:
Let $sc_t(n)$ be the number of self-conjugate $t$-core partitions of $n$, let $sc(n)$ be the number of self-conjugate partitions of $n$, and define

$$
\sigma_t(n)=\frac{sc_{t+2}(n)-sc_t(n)}{sc(n)}.
$$

For fixed $n\geq 139$, the sequence $\{\sigma_{2t}(n)\}_{8\leq 2t\leq 2\lfloor n/4\rfloor-8}$ is considered, and for fixed $n\geq 213$, the sequence $\{\sigma_{2t+1}(n)\}_{9\leq 2t+1\leq\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ is considered. **Unimodality conjecture for normalized self-conjugate core increments.** Both sequences are unimodal. The source reports partial results but says that the main work remains open.
object.source_name: Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Rishi Nath, “The number of self-conjugate core partitions”, arXiv:1201.6629 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.6629

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2012). “We state this as an open question.”

object.title: Factorisation of the supersymmetry singlet norm
object.statement: For twist angle $\phi=\pi$, write the supersymmetry singlet as $|\Psi\rangle=\sum_\mu\psi_\mu|\mu\rangle$, with the components chosen as coprime polynomials in $x,y$. **The norm-factorisation conjecture.** The square norm $\lVert\Psi\rVert^2$ factorises into two polynomials in $x,y$; when $N$ is odd, one factor is the component $\psi_{11\cdots1}$. This is an observed sum rule for the singlet states.
object.source_name: Christian Hagendorf, “Spin chains with dynamical lattice supersymmetry”, arXiv:1207.0357 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0357

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2012). “The present work leads to many open questions.”

object.title: Tree-symmetrization identity for the Joyce potential
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be an unrooted, unlabeled tree with $n$ vertices, and let $K_\mathcal{T}(\{\gamma_i,t_i\})$ be the tree kernel defined by the product over its oriented edges. Write ${\rm Sym}$ for symmetrization over the labels. For each labeling $\ell:v\mapsto i\in[1,n]$ of the vertices, orient every edge from $v$ to $v'$ whenever $\ell(v)<\ell(v')$. **Tree-symmetrization conjecture.** For each unrooted, unlabeled tree $\mathcal{T}$ one has

$$
{\rm Sym}\,K_\mathcal{T}(\{\gamma_i,t_i\})=\frac{1}{(4\pi\mathrm{i})^{n-1}}\,{\rm Sym}\,\Biggl[\left(\sum_{\rm labels}\prod_{e:i\to j}\langle\gamma_i,\gamma_j\rangle\right)\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{t_i t_{i+1}}{t_{i+1}-t_i}\Biggr].
$$

The identity is proposed to establish that the tree expansion of the Fourier modes of the Joyce potential agrees with the expression obtained from the Joyce construction, thereby relating the factorized and tree-based descriptions of the heavenly metric.
object.source_name: Sergei Alexandrov and Boris Pioline, “Heavenly metrics, BPS indices and twistors”, arXiv:2104.10540 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.10540

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

object.title: The odd-width admissible-partition character identity for $C_{(1)}_\ell$
object.statement:
Let $\ell\geq 2$. Let $\mathcal N_{2\ell+1}$ be the array of $\ell$ copies of $\mathbb N$ together with the odd positive integers, arranged in $2\ell+1$ rows, and let $f_a$ denote the frequency of the part $a$ in a colored partition. For parameters $k_0,\dots,k_\ell$, write $k=k_0+\cdots+k_\ell$, and let $D(k_0+1,k_1+1,\dots,k_\ell+1)$ and $\Delta(k_1+1,\dots,k_\ell+1)$ denote the indexing sets used in the principally specialized character.

**The odd-width character identity.** The principally specialized character

$$
\frac{\prod_{a\in\{0\}^\ell\cup D(k_0+1, k_1+1,\dots, k_\ell+1);\, b\in \Delta( k_1+1,\dots, k_\ell+1);\, j\equiv a,\pm b\mod (2\ell+2k+2)}(1-q^j)}{\prod_{j\, \text{odd}}(1-q^j)\prod_{j\in\mathbb N}(1-q^j)^\ell}
$$

is the generating function for the number of $(k_0,k_1,\dots,k_\ell)$-admissible colored partitions

$$
n=\sum_{a\in\mathcal N_{2\ell+1}}f_a\cdot a.
$$

This identity connects principally specialized $C_\ell^{(1)}$-characters with colored-partition generating functions; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: S. Capparelli, A. Meurman, A. Primc and M. Primc, “New Partition Identities From C_^(1)-Modules”, arXiv:2106.06262 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06262

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

object.title: The analytic torsion formula for Shannon products with complete graphs
object.statement:
Let $C_n$ be a circle and $K_m$ a complete graph, with $C_n * K_m$ their Shannon product. **The complete-graph product conjecture.**

$$
A(C_n * K_m) = n^2/m.
$$

This is presented as an experimentally observed formula for homotopy cylinders; the paper does not provide a proof.
object.source_name: Oliver Knill, “Analytic torsion for graphs”, arXiv:2201.09412 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09412

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: The analytic torsion formula for Shannon products with linear graphs
object.statement:
Let $C_n$ be a circle and $L_n$ a linear graph with $n$ vertices, with $C_n * L_n$ their Shannon product. **The linear-graph product conjecture.**

$$
A(C_n * L_n) = n^2 m/(3m-2).
$$

The notation is inconsistent: the left-hand side uses $L_n$, while the right-hand side contains $m$. The supplied text gives no supporting discussion or proof.
object.source_name: Oliver Knill, “Analytic torsion for graphs”, arXiv:2201.09412 (2022).
object.references:

object.title: The cubic Borwein sign-pattern conjecture
object.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and define

$$
P_n(q):=(1-q)(1-q^2)(1-q^4)(1-q^5)\cdots(1-q^{3n-2})(1-q^{3n-1}).
$$

**Cubic Borwein conjecture.** The sign pattern of the coefficients in the expansion of $P_n(q)^3$ is $+--+--+--\cdots$, with the same convention concerning zero coefficients as above. The source describes this as only partially proved.
object.source_name: Chen Wang and Christian Krattenthaler, “An asymptotic approach to Borwein-type sign pattern theorems”, arXiv:2201.12415 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12415

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: The Catalan-array conjecture for vertically-recurrent matrices
object.statement: Let $C_n$ denote the Catalan triangular array. A matrix is **vertically recurrent** when it satisfies the paper's vertical recurrence relation. **The Catalan-array conjecture.** The Catalan array $C_n$ is a vertically-recurrent matrix. This conjecture asserts that the Catalan array belongs to the class of vertically-recurrent matrices; the supplied text gives no resolution or supporting result.
object.source_name: Hossein Teimoori Faal, “On Vertically-Recurrent Matrices and Their Algebraic Properties”, arXiv:2206.02758 (2022).
object.references:

object.title: The fully reducible Venn diagram converse conjecture
object.statement:
Let $V$ be a simple $m$-dimensional $n$-Venn diagram. A diagram is **fully reducible** if it has the reduction property defined in the paper.

**Fully reducible Venn diagram converse conjecture.** If $n\leq m+1$, then $V$ is fully reducible.

The conjecture is the converse of the preceding theorem, which proves that full reducibility implies $n\leq m+1$.
object.source_name: Mohammad Farrokhi Derakhshandeh Ghouchan, “Fully reducible simple Venn diagrams”, arXiv:2206.03323 (2022).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

object.title: Stanley's chromatic conjecture for trees
object.statement:
Let $T$ and $U$ be trees, and let $X_T$ and $X_U$ denote their chromatic symmetric functions.

**Stanley's chromatic conjecture for trees.** Trees $T$ and $U$ are isomorphic as graphs if and only if

$$
X_T=X_U.
$$

This is an open problem asking whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees up to graph isomorphism.
object.source_name: Nicholas A. Loehr and Gregory S. Warrington, “A rooted variant of Stanley's chromatic symmetric function”, arXiv:2206.05392 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05392

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2022). “The influential paper contains an open problem that we call Stanley's Chromatic Conjecture for Trees:”

object.title: Extremal bound for suboptimal $(2d+1)$-union antichains
object.statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $\mathcal{L}(V)$ denote its lattice of subspaces. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{L}(V)$ is a **$(2d+1)$-union antichain** if it is an antichain whose union of any $2d+1$ members is not a member of the family. Assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is not contained in any optimal $(2d+1)$-union antichain and that $2d+1<n$. Let $\left[n\atop d\right]$ denote the Gaussian binomial coefficient and let $\mathcal{B}[n,2d+1]$ be the family defined in the source. **Extremal bound conjecture.**

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \left[n\atop d\right]-q\left[d\atop 1\right].
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{B}[n,2d+1]$. This conjecture seeks the sharp size bound and equality characterization for suboptimal $(2d+1)$-union antichains; the notation $\mathcal{B}[n,2d+1]$ is not defined in the supplied context, and its structure and the conjecture's resolution require verification.
object.source_name: Yunjing Shan and Junling Zhou, “Suboptimal s-union familes and s-union antichains for vector spaces”, arXiv:2207.06727 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.06727

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

object.title: Clark's conjecture on even Zumkeller numbers
object.statement: An integer is **Zumkeller** if its positive divisors can be partitioned into two sets with equal sum, and it is **half-Zumkeller** if it satisfies the paper's corresponding half-Zumkeller condition. **Clark's conjecture.** If $n$ is an even Zumkeller number, then $n$ is half-Zumkeller. The conjecture was raised by the authors cited as Clark; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Farid Jokar, “On k-layered numbers”, arXiv:2207.09053 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.09053

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2022). “Although it is an open question that for every positive integer $k$, there exists a $k$-layered numbers, but Table and Remark lead us to the following conjecture.”

object.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the Paley–Wiener extremal problem below $p=1$
object.statement: For $0<p<\infty$, consider the extremal problem defining the Paley–Wiener extremal function, and call a function attaining the extremum a **solution**. **Uniqueness conjecture.** The extremal problem has a unique solution for $0<p<1$. The source describes this as the most basic unresolved problem about the extremal functions.
object.source_name: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Andrés Chirre, Joaquim Ortega-Cerdà and Kristian Seip, “Point evaluation in Paley–Wiener spaces”, arXiv:2210.13922 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Evenness conjecture for Paley–Wiener extremal functions
object.statement: Let $0<p<1$, and let a **solution** mean a function solving the extremal problem defined earlier in the paper. **Evenness conjecture.** Any solution of the extremal problem is even. The claim is motivated by the observation that uniqueness would force evenness, but the source presents evenness itself as a separate, presumably easier problem.
object.source_name: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Andrés Chirre, Joaquim Ortega-Cerdà and Kristian Seip, “Point evaluation in Paley–Wiener spaces”, arXiv:2210.13922 (2023).

object.title: Gessel's equidistribution conjecture for permutations with disjoint cycle types
object.statement:
Let $\mu\vdash m$ and $\nu\vdash n$ be integer partitions with no common part. Let $\pi$ and $\sigma$ be permutations of cycle types $\mu$ and $\nu$, respectively, with disjoint supports. Let $A_{\pi,\sigma}$ be the subset of the conjugacy class of cycle type $\mu\sqcup\nu\vdash m+n$ consisting of the permutations for which the relative order of the letters in the union of all cycles of $\mu$ is as in $\pi$, and the relative order of the letters in the union of all cycles of $\nu$ is as in $\sigma$. **Gessel's conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum\limits_{w\in A_{\pi,\sigma}} {\bf x}^{\Des(w)}=\sum\limits_{\tau\in \pi\shuffle \sigma} {\bf x}^{\Des(\tau)}.
$$

This equidistribution identity connects descent enumerators on a constrained conjugacy class with those on shuffles of the two permutations. The conjecture was proved by Gessel, so it is included as a solved result.
object.source_name: Ron M. Adin and Yuval Roichman, “Cyclic descents, matchings and Schur-positivity”, arXiv:2210.14839 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.14839

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2022). “Conjecture was proved by Gessel.”

object.title: Akbari–Ashrafi conjecture on connected reduced power graphs of simple groups
object.statement: Let $G$ be a non-abelian simple group. The **Akbari–Ashrafi conjecture.** The reduced power graph of $G$ is connected only if $G$ is isomorphic to an alternating group $A_n$. This conjecture concerns connectivity in reduced power graphs; the supplied context does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Yilong Yang, “Reduced Power Graphs of PGL_3(F_q)”, arXiv:2306.13314 (2023).
object.references:

object.title: Vertex-deletion conjecture for the upper orientable total domination number
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph in $\mathcal{C}$ and let $v\in V(G)$ be such that $G-v\in\mathcal{C}$. **Vertex-deletion conjecture.**

$$
{\rm DOM}_t(G)\leq {\rm DOM}_t(G-v)+1.
$$

The conjecture proposes the missing lower bound from the cited vertex-deletion result; the corresponding upper bound for induced subgraphs is known, but this inequality was not proved in the paper.
object.source_name: Sarah E. Anderson, Tanja Dravec, Daniel Johnston and Kirsti Kuenzel, “Orientable total domination in graphs”, arXiv:2311.16307 (2023).
object.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16307

object.title: The Abrams–Tomforde conjecture for Leavitt path algebras and graph $C^*$-algebras
object.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be graphs and let $\mathsf{k}$ be a field. Consider the Leavitt path algebras $L_\mathsf{k}(E)$ and $L_\mathsf{k}(F)$, and the graph $C^*$-algebras $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$. **Abrams–Tomforde conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $L_\mathsf{k}(E)$ and $L_\mathsf{k}(F)$ are isomorphic as rings.
2. $C^*(E)$ and $C^*(F)$ are isomorphic as $C^*$-algebras.

This conjecture, posed in 2011, seeks to characterize when the algebraic and analytic graph-algebra constructions have the same isomorphism classification. The parser supplies no resolution evidence, so it is recorded as open.
object.source_name: Gene Abrams and Roozbeh Hazrat, “Monoids, dynamics and Leavitt path algebras”, arXiv:2409.00289 (2024).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1610.02232](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.02232), [arXiv:1204.3366](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.3366).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00289

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

object.title: The square-grid error-correcting locating-dominating set density conjecture
object.statement:
Let $SQ$ denote the infinite square grid, and let $\textrm{ERR:LD}(SQ)$ denote its error-correcting locating-dominating set density. **Square-grid density conjecture.**

$$
\textrm{ERR:LD}(SQ)=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

The authors state that this value is strongly suggested by their examination, but that no proof is known; the conjecture concerns the tight density bound for the square grid.
object.source_name: Devin Jean and Suk Seo, “Fault-Tolerant Locating-Dominating sets with Error-correction”, arXiv:2212.08193 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08193

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
